unsupported_claims.claim: A callback is scheduled if the caller accepts it.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The callback process is labeled “Offer callback; schedule if accepted,” and the reconstruction repeats scheduling as an outcome and constraint.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief requires offering a callback instead of holding indefinitely, but it does not explicitly specify an acceptance decision or scheduling behavior. Scheduling is plausible operational detail, but it is additional specificity.

unsupported_claims.claim: Review inputs are selected through a distinct flagged-calls mechanism.
unsupported_claims.reconstruction_evidence: The reconstruction says “Select ‘Flagged calls’ from Recordings + transcripts” and send them to the review process.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The brief says unresolved and abandoned calls feed review, but it does not define a separate flagging component, selection mechanism, or classification stage. The reconstruction itself notes that the flagging rule and owner are not shown.

verdict.strongest_transmitted_behavior: The strongest transmission is the complete operational routing story: caller-number lookup branches to personalized or generic intake, consent and speech/keypad intent capture lead to AI eligibility, routine calls reach bounded AI self-service, all three escalation triggers converge on the human queue, and wait-target failure produces a callback path.
verdict.most_consequential_loss: The most consequential loss is the absence of the explicit real-time conversational requirement for the AI voice agent. The low-confidence trigger is also communicated only as “low confidence,” without preserving that it is the agent's own risk flag.
verdict.overall_summary: The reconstruction is highly faithful and engineering-usable. It recovers the system boundaries, major components, ownership, ordered intake flow, lookup degradation, keypad fallback, AI capability constraints, human escalation triggers, handoff payload, wait-target callback behavior, call-wide evidence capture, and the review feedback loop. No system-defining flow is contradicted, and the main end-to-end process is complete. Fidelity falls short of near-exact because the real-time interaction constraint is absent, the risk-flag semantics are softened, the limited action-set constraint is conveyed indirectly, and two small operational details are added beyond the brief.
